_meta.source: docs/design/RICE-GUIDE.md (desktop-authoritative) + docs/design/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md §2 (full ramps, unchanged bg/border companions for alert tones)
_meta.note: Single source of truth for rice colour. Edit here and rerun generate_theme.py -- never hand-edit a hex in an app config (RICE-GUIDE.md, 'Working rules for Claude Code'). Where RICE-GUIDE.md and DESIGN-SYSTEM.md differ for desktop use, RICE-GUIDE.md wins -- see cursor/selection/ANSI-cyan below.

_verdigris_note: Terminal-only extension (RICE-GUIDE.md 'Terminal extension'). Fills the cyan ANSI slots the core palette has no family for. Never use as a UI accent in bars/launchers/window chrome.

geometry._note: Non-colour tokens. GTK3 (waybar, wofi, wlogout) has no CSS custom properties, so these cannot be emitted as variables the way colours are -- each GTK3 stylesheet carries the literal with a comment pointing here. swaync is GTK4 and does read them as variables; Hyprland reads rounding from the generated palette.lua.

typography._note: The GTK/Qt row of RICE-GUIDE.md's typography table, plus the mono face for Qt's fixed-width slot. Only KDE consumes these: kdeglobals is where Qt applications read their font, and KDE's gtkconfig daemon copies the same values into the GTK settings.ini files. Everything else here sets its font in its own config, because font mixes with structural settings.
typography._weight_note: kde_weight is the Qt 0-99 scale KDE still writes in kdeglobals, not the CSS scale: 57 is Medium and matches geometry.font_weight_ui of 500. Writing 500 there is silently clamped and renders as Black.
